growing_tip.body_text: Peas (Sweet) | → Super sugar snap: widely available, earlier, resistant to powdery mildew → Sugar snap: productive, delicious, resistant to some diseases, but not mildew A mixture of the two varieties is ideal as you can benefit from the qualities each one has to offer: the earliness of the Super sugar and the abundance and taste of the Sugar. → *2 rows (18”-45 cm) per bed spaced every 0,5” (13 mm) along the row. → Earthway seeder: Jumbo peas plate, 2-3 passages. Seed into 1” (2.5cm) deep furrow *When planting more than one bed side by side, adjust density to 1 row per bed (leaving enough room between the beds for comfortable harvesting). → Like beans, peas will do best in beds amended with compost, fresh or aged. Rule of thumb is to spread 1 inch (5 cm) in the middle of the bed. → When planting in beds where compost was applied in the previous crops, we only supplement with a mixture of alfalfa meal (2-0-2) and pelleted chicken manure (5-3-2). Add this extra fertility boost at first cultivation 3-4 weeks after the direct sown date. → Inoculants can increase yields by promoting a rhizobium-pea symbiosis that facilitates nitrogen fixation. If nitrogen-fixing nodules are not found on most legumes grown in a specific planting area (ie new beds), inoculants are added to the seeds when sowing. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions. 1 | → Install irrigation and water until the soil is deeply moistened. Keep moist for the next 7–10 days until all seeds have germinated. Once the seeds have germinated, favour drip irrigation over overhead if the plants need watering. → Start some extra seedlings in the greenhouse to fill in the holes on the beds. Ideally, these should be started in the week prior to when the direct seeding is done. → Minimum soil temperature is 15°C (20°C is optimal). If seeded in soil that is too cold, cover seedbed with clear plastic one week prior to seeding date * If the previous crop is too well established, or if the bed is too messy, mow the previ...

irrigation.body_text: → Drip tape only (2 per bed) → No sprinkler to keep foliage and pods dry and thus prevent diseases | → Root depth: Shallow (6”-24”) → General: Can drink lots of water because they are fast growing. Vulnerable to disease with overhead water. Sweet peas are a very popular crop with customers, especially in early spring when they’re taste is incredible. Like beans, peas have low productivity rates being timeconsuming to harvest. To grow this crop profitability, we ensure the plants are properly fertilized, have the right amount of Rhizobium, are rigorously staked and trellised, and are harvested often. For a continuous supply, we seed new beds every 4 weeks → Rotary harrow → 30” bed prep rake → Direct Seeding: Hands or Earthway seeder (+ jumbo bean plate). 2 tubes for the rake, scale, notepad and your seeds → Transplanting: Popping tray → Remove tarp and clean out large debris. Use the rake if needed.* → If adding compost, uniformly apply it in the center and pass with the rotary harrow at a depth of 1.5” (4 cm). Use the rake to remove debris if needed. Otherwise, the bed is ready to be seeded. → Mark your 2 rows with the bed prep rake, pressing hard to create a furrow at least 1’’ deep (5cm) and seed with your hands by rolling the seeds close to another on the furrow. → Write down the total amount of seed dropped onto the first bed and comparing with the target. Adjust calibration if required. → If using the Earthway, 2 or 3 passes will be required to obtain the desired density. 2
